designs.Problem:
Design a 32-bit adder with carry-in and carry-out.

Module Name: adder_32bit_carry
Inputs:
  - a[31:0]: first 32-bit operand
  - b[31:0]: second 32-bit operand
  - cin: carry input
Outputs:
  - sum[31:0]: 32-bit sum output
  - cout: carry output

The design should compute sum = a + b + cin, with cout being the carry generated by the addition. Combinational logic only, no clock.
designs.Module header:
module adder_32bit_carry (
    input  [31:0] a,
    input  [31:0] b,
    input         cin,
    output [31:0] sum,
    output        cout
);
designs.fabric_hint: For the addition, use full-vector arithmetic operators (e.g. '+') rather than manually decomposed bit-level carry logic, so the synthesis tool can map the addition onto dedicated fast-carry hardware.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate 8 CARRY4 primitives chained together (CO[3] of instance i feeding CI of instance i+1, with CI of the first instance tied to cin) to implement the 32-bit addition, per the CARRY4 template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above. Compute per-bit propagate (P = a ^ b) and generate (G = a & b) signals and wire them to the S and DI inputs of each CARRY4 instance; the final CO of the last instance is cout, and the O outputs concatenated form sum.

designs.Problem:
Design a 16x16-bit unsigned combinational multiplier.

Module Name: mult_16x16_unsigned
Inputs:
  - a[15:0]: first unsigned operand
  - b[15:0]: second unsigned operand
Outputs:
  - product[31:0]: unsigned product of a and b

The design should compute product = a * b. Combinational logic only, no clock.
designs.fabric_hint: Use the '*' operator directly on the full-width operands rather than describing partial-product generation and addition manually, so the synthesis tool can map the multiplication onto a dedicated hardware multiplier block.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate a DSP48E1 primitive to compute the 16x16 unsigned multiplication, per Template A (Fully Combinational Multiplier) in the FPGA fabric knowledge above. Zero-extend a to the 30-bit A input and b to the 18-bit B input, configure OPMODE/ALUMODE for a pure multiply (no accumulation), and slice the lower 32 bits of the 48-bit P output as product. Because CLK is tied to 1'b0 (no clock), you MUST bypass ALL eleven register-enable parameters to 0 (AREG, ACASCREG, BREG, BCASCREG, CREG, MREG, PREG, ADREG, DREG, INMODEREG, ALUMODEREG, OPMODEREG, CARRYINREG, CARRYINSELREG) exactly as shown in Template A -- do not omit OPMODEREG, it is easy to forget. You MUST also explicitly wire every DSP48E1 input port with no exceptions, including .CARRYIN(1'b0) and .D(25'b0); leaving CARRYIN unconnected while CARRYINREG=0 injects X into every bit of P even when A/B/C are valid.

designs.Problem:
Design an 8x8-bit unsigned multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit.

Module Name: mac_8x8_accum
Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - rst: synchronous active-high reset, clears the accumulator
  - accum_en: when high, on each rising clk edge add a*b into the accumulator
  - a[7:0]: first unsigned operand
  - b[7:0]: second unsigned operand
Outputs:
  - acc[19:0]: accumulator register, holding the running sum of a*b products

On reset, acc must synchronously clear to 0. When accum_en is high, acc <= acc + a*b on each rising edge of clk; when accum_en is low, acc holds its value. Clock frequency target: 100 MHz (10 ns period).
designs.Module header:
module mac_8x8_accum (
    input             clk,
    input             rst,
    input             accum_en,
    input  [7:0]      a,
    input  [7:0]      b,
    output reg [19:0] acc
);
designs.fabric_hint: Keep the multiply and the accumulation together in the same synchronous always block (e.g. acc <= acc + a*b), rather than splitting them into a separate multiplier and a separate adder, so the synthesis tool can map the multiply-accumulate onto a single dedicated DSP datapath.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate a DSP48E1 primitive to implement the multiply-accumulate, per Template B (Synchronous Multiply-Accumulator) in the FPGA fabric knowledge above. Wire a and b (zero-extended) to A/B, use CLK for clk, configure OPMODE/ALUMODE so P accumulates a*b into itself each cycle when accum_en is asserted (gate the relevant clock-enable port with accum_en), and use RSTP (or equivalent reset behavior) driven by rst to synchronously clear the accumulator. IMPORTANT: PREG(1) already makes P a registered signal (it updates on the same clock edge that latches the new accumulated value), so acc MUST be exposed as a COMBINATIONAL slice of P's lower 20 bits (e.g. always @(*) acc = accum_wide[19:0];), never re-registered with a second always @(posedge clk) block -- doing so adds a second cycle of latency and every result will read back exactly one cycle late.

designs.Problem:
Design a 16-to-1 multiplexer.

Module Name: mux16to1
Inputs:
  - data_in[15:0]: 16 single-bit data inputs
  - sel[3:0]: 4-bit select
Outputs:
  - data_out: selected bit, data_out = data_in[sel]

Combinational logic only, no clock.
designs.fabric_hint: Describe the selection logic with a single case statement (or a direct indexed bit-select) over the full select vector, rather than a manually unrolled tree of 2:1 multiplexers, so the synthesis tool can pack the wide multiplexer onto dedicated per-slice mux hardware.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate one MUXF7 primitive to combine two behaviorally-described 8:1 halves, per the MUXF7 template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above. Build data_in[7:0] selected by sel[2:0] as one 8:1 half (I0) and data_in[15:8] selected by sel[2:0] as the other 8:1 half (I1) using ordinary case/if-else logic, then wire the MUXF7's S input to sel[3] and its O output to data_out.

designs.Problem:
Design a 32-stage serial shift register.

Module Name: shift_reg_32_srl
Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - shift_en: when high, shift serial_in into the register on each rising clk edge
  - serial_in: serial data input
Outputs:
  - serial_out: output of the last (32nd) stage, i.e. data delayed by 32 clock cycles

Only the final-stage output needs to be observable; intermediate taps do not need to be exposed. Clock frequency target: 100 MHz (10 ns period).
designs.fabric_hint: Model the shift register as a single synchronous shift of a vector (e.g. shreg <= {shreg[N-2:0], serial_in};) with a uniform clock and enable, rather than mixing per-bit reset/enable logic, so the synthesis tool can pack it into a dedicated LUT-based shift-register primitive instead of discrete flip-flops.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate one SRLC32E primitive to implement the 32-stage shift register, per the SRLC32E template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above. Wire D to serial_in, CE to shift_en, CLK to clk, tie A to 5'd31 (the fixed 32-stage tap address), and connect serial_out to the Q31 output (the fixed-delay tap), since only the final stage needs to be observable.

designs.Problem:
Design a 32x8 single-port RAM (32 addressable locations, 8 bits wide) with synchronous write and asynchronous (combinational) read, implemented with minimum Block RAM (BRAM) usage -- i.e. the synthesis tool should map the memory onto distributed RAM (LUT-based SelectRAM) rather than a dedicated RAMB18E1/RAMB36E1 block.

Module Name: ram32x8_distributed
Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - we: write enable, when high writes din into mem[addr] on the rising clk edge
  - addr[4:0]: 5-bit address (32 locations)
  - din[7:0]: 8-bit data input
Outputs:
  - dout[7:0]: 8-bit data output, dout = mem[addr] (combinational/asynchronous read)

The read must be purely combinational (dout must reflect mem[addr] immediately, with no clocked output register), and the write must be synchronous (only committed on the rising edge of clk when we is high). Clock frequency target: 100 MHz (10 ns period).
designs.Module header:
module ram32x8_distributed (
    input        clk,
    input        we,
    input  [4:0] addr,
    input  [7:0] din,
    output [7:0] dout
);
designs.fabric_hint: Describe the memory as a small 32-entry, 8-bit-wide register array with synchronous write and purely combinational (asynchronous) read (e.g. reg [7:0] mem [0:31]; always @(posedge clk) if (we) mem[addr] <= din; assign dout = mem[addr];), rather than a registered/synchronous-read style, so the synthesis tool maps it onto LUT-based distributed RAM (SelectRAM) instead of a dedicated Block RAM tile.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate 8 RAM32X1S primitives (one per output data bit), per the RAM32X1S template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above. All 8 instances share the same 5-bit address (A0-A4 wired to addr[0]-addr[4]), WCLK wired to clk, and WE wired to we; wire each instance's D to din[i] and O to dout[i] for i = 0..7 (a generate loop is idiomatic here). Vivado's report_utilization reports these structurally-instantiated instances as RAM32X1S (Ref Name, Functional Category 'Distributed Memory'), which is checked via expected_primitives (RAMS32 >= 8, with RAM32X1S accepted as an alias of the same underlying distributed-RAM hardware) in addition to the resource_caps hard constraint (RAMB18E1 = 0, RAMB36E1 = 0) confirming no block RAM was used.

designs.Problem:
Design a 16x16-bit unsigned combinational multiplier that does NOT use any dedicated DSP hardware multiplier block.

Module Name: mult_16x16_no_dsp
Inputs:
  - a[15:0]: first unsigned operand
  - b[15:0]: second unsigned operand
Outputs:
  - product[31:0]: unsigned product of a and b

The design should compute product = a * b using only general FPGA fabric logic (LUTs and fast-carry chains) -- the target device's DSP48E1 slices must NOT be used for this design. Combinational logic only, no clock.
designs.fabric_hint: Compute the product using ordinary Verilog arithmetic (the '*' operator) or an explicit shift-and-add / partial-product accumulation loop over full-width vectors. The '*' operator alone does not guarantee DSP inference is avoided under every Vivado synthesis strategy, so if you observe DSP48E1 usage, restructure the arithmetic as an explicit shift-and-add accumulation of 16 partial products using plain adders instead, so the synthesis tool maps the arithmetic onto general LUT logic and fast-carry (CARRY4) chains rather than a dedicated DSP48E1 hardware multiplier.
designs.primitive_hint: Do not structurally instantiate a DSP48E1 for this design. Instead, generate the 16 partial products (a AND-ed with each bit of b, shifted appropriately) and sum them with an explicit adder tree, structurally instantiating CARRY4 primitives (per the CARRY4 template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above) for the accumulation stages, so Vivado maps the arithmetic onto LUT logic and fast-carry chains instead of a DSP slice.

Design a 64-bit adder with carry-in and carry-out.

Module Name: adder_64bit_carry
Inputs:
  - a[63:0]: first 64-bit operand
  - b[63:0]: second 64-bit operand
  - cin: carry input
Outputs:
  - sum[63:0]: 64-bit sum output
  - cout: carry output

The design should compute sum = a + b + cin, with cout being the carry generated by the addition. Combinational logic only, no clock.
designs.Module header:
module adder_64bit_carry (

designs.fabric_hint: For the addition, use full-vector arithmetic operators (e.g. '+') rather than manually decomposed bit-level carry logic, so the synthesis tool can map the addition onto dedicated fast-carry hardware.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate 16 CARRY4 primitives chained together (CO[3] of instance i feeding CI of instance i+1, with CI of the first instance tied to cin) to implement the 64-bit addition, per the CARRY4 template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above. designs.Problem:
Design a single FIR-filter tap that combines a 32-cycle sample delay line with a multiply-accumulate datapath.

Module Name: fir_tap_srl_dsp
Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - rst: synchronous active-high reset, clears the accumulator (the delay line itself is not reset, matching real shift-register-LUT hardware which has no reset input)
  - shift_en: when high, shift sample_in into the 32-stage delay line on each rising clk edge
  - accum_en: when high, on each rising clk edge add (delayed_sample * coeff) into the accumulator, where delayed_sample is the current output of the 32-stage delay line (the sample that was shifted in 32 cycles earlier)
  - sample_in[7:0]: unsigned sample input, shifted into the delay line each cycle when shift_en is high
  - coeff[7:0]: unsigned FIR tap coefficient
Outputs:
  - acc[19:0]: accumulator register, holding the running sum of (delayed_sample * coeff) products

On reset, acc must synchronously clear to 0. This design is intentionally clocked at a tight period (see Clock Constraint) to exercise post-synthesis timing analysis in addition to fabric-primitive checks.
designs.Module header:
module fir_tap_srl_dsp (
    input             clk,
    input             rst,
    input             shift_en,
    input             accum_en,
    input  [7:0]      sample_in,
    input  [7:0]      coeff,
    output reg [19:0] acc
);
designs.fabric_hint: Implement the delay line as 8 independent 1-bit shift registers, one per bit of sample_in (e.g. via a generate/genvar loop over bit index k, each following the exact same single-bit shift idiom as shift_reg_32_srl: shreg_k <= {shreg_k[30:0], sample_in[k]}; delayed_sample[k] = shreg_k[31];), rather than describing the delay line as a single 2D array of 8-bit words -- this is what reliably lets Vivado's shift-register extraction pack each bit lane into its own SRLC32E primitive (8 total) instead of discrete flip-flops. Keep the multiply-accumulate in a single synchronous always block (acc <= acc + delayed_sample*coeff), exactly as in mac_8x8_accum, so it maps onto a single dedicated DSP48E1 datapath.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate 8 SRLC32E primitives (one per bit of sample_in, per the SRLC32E template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above) -- for bit k, wire D to sample_in[k], CE to shift_en, CLK to clk, A tied to 5'd31, and Q31 to delayed_sample[k] -- and explicitly instantiate one DSP48E1 primitive (per Template B, Synchronous Multiply-Accumulator) to compute the multiply-accumulate: wire delayed_sample and coeff (zero-extended) to A/B, CLK to clk, configure OPMODE/ALUMODE so P accumulates delayed_sample*coeff into itself each cycle when accum_en is asserted, and use RSTP driven by rst to synchronously clear the accumulator. IMPORTANT (same pitfall as mac_8x8_accum): PREG(1) already registers P, so acc MUST be exposed as a COMBINATIONAL slice of P's lower 20 bits, never re-registered with a second always @(posedge clk) block.

designs.Problem:
Design a 256x16 single-port RAM (256 addressable locations, 16 bits wide, 4Kbit total) with synchronous write and synchronous (registered) read, sized so the synthesis tool should map the memory onto a dedicated Block RAM tile (RAMB18E1/RAMB36E1) rather than distributed RAM or a flat bank of discrete flip-flops.

Module Name: ram256x16_bram
Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - we: write enable, when high writes din into mem[addr] on the rising clk edge
  - addr[7:0]: 8-bit address (256 locations)
  - din[15:0]: 16-bit data input
Outputs:
  - dout[15:0]: 16-bit data output, registered so that dout reflects mem[addr] one clock cycle after addr is presented (synchronous read)

The read must be registered/synchronous (dout updates on the rising clk edge to the value of mem[addr] as addr was presented just before that edge, with no combinational/asynchronous read path), and the write must be synchronous (only committed on the rising edge of clk when we is high). Clock frequency target: 100 MHz (10 ns period).
designs.Module header:
module ram256x16_bram (
    input         clk,
    input         we,
    input  [7:0]  addr,
    input  [15:0] din,
    output reg [15:0] dout
);
designs.fabric_hint: Describe the memory as a 256-entry, 16-bit-wide register array with synchronous write AND the read registered in the SAME synchronous always block as the write (e.g. reg [15:0] mem [0:255]; always @(posedge clk) begin if (we) mem[addr] <= din; dout <= mem[addr]; end), rather than a combinational/asynchronous read style (assign dout = mem[addr];), so the synthesis tool maps it onto a dedicated Block RAM tile (RAMB18E1/RAMB36E1) instead of distributed RAM or discrete flip-flops.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate one RAMB18E1 primitive, per the RAMB18E1 template (Section 10.6) in the FPGA fabric knowledge above, configured in its native 18-bit-wide/1024-deep mode. Zero-pad the 8-bit addr into the 14-bit ADDRARDADDR bus aligned to bits [13:4] (with [3:0] tied to 0), wire din to DIADI and dout to DOADO, tie DIPADIP to 2'b00, set DOA_REG(1) so the read output is registered (matching this design's one-cycle synchronous read latency), and tie off every Port B input (ENBWREN(1'b0), DIBDI/DIPBDIP/ADDRBWRADDR to 0, etc.) since only one read/write port is needed.

designs.Problem:
Design an 8-input combinational reduction adder that sums eight unsigned 8-bit operands into a single wider result.

Module Name: wide_reduce_flexible_arch
Inputs:
  - in0[7:0], in1[7:0], in2[7:0], in3[7:0], in4[7:0], in5[7:0], in6[7:0], in7[7:0]: eight unsigned 8-bit operands
Outputs:
  - sum[10:0]: 11-bit unsigned sum of all eight operands (wide enough to hold the maximum possible sum, 8 x 255 = 2040)

The design should compute sum = in0 + in1 + in2 + in3 + in4 + in5 + in6 + in7. Combinational logic only, no clock.
designs.Module header:
module wide_reduce_flexible_arch (
    input  [7:0] in0,
    input  [7:0] in1,
    input  [7:0] in2,
    input  [7:0] in3,
    input  [7:0] in4,
    input  [7:0] in5,
    input  [7:0] in6,
    input  [7:0] in7,
    output [10:0] sum
);
designs.fabric_hint: Compute the 8-input sum using ordinary Verilog '+' operators over the full-width operands (e.g. a straightforward reduction such as sum = in0+in1+in2+in3+in4+in5+in6+in7;). This design intentionally accepts either a pure fabric-logic adder tree (mapped onto CARRY4 fast-carry chains) or, under the explicit_primitive generation style, a DSP48E1-based accumulation chain -- both are equally valid, fabric-efficient implementations of this reduction; you do not need to force one over the other.
designs.primitive_hint: If generating structurally (explicit_primitive style), you may EITHER build the reduction from CARRY4 fast-carry adder chains (per the CARRY4 template above, as in the 32-bit/64-bit adder examples), OR structurally instantiate a chain of DSP48E1 primitives configured as pure adders (bypass the multiplier stage, set ALUMODE/OPMODE for addition, and feed each DSP's C input from the running partial sum, cascading e.g. 2-3 DSP48E1 instances to combine groups of the 8 operands). Either architecture is an acceptable, fabric-efficient solution for this design.

designs.Problem:
Design a 16x16-bit unsigned synchronous (registered) multiplier: a single-cycle pipeline stage that registers the product on each rising clock edge.

Module Name: mult_16x16_dsp_registered
Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - a[15:0]: first unsigned operand
  - b[15:0]: second unsigned operand
Outputs:
  - product[31:0]: registered unsigned product of a and b, updated on each rising clk edge (one cycle of latency)

On each rising edge of clk, product must update to the product of the a and b values sampled at that same edge. Clock frequency target: 100 MHz (10 ns period).
designs.fabric_hint: Register the product directly in a synchronous always block (e.g. always @(posedge clk) product <= a * b;) rather than computing the multiply combinationally and adding a separate output register, so the synthesis tool maps both the multiply and the output register onto a single DSP48E1's internal pipeline register.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate a DSP48E1 primitive to compute the registered 16x16 unsigned multiplication, per Template A (Fully Combinational Multiplier) in the FPGA fabric knowledge above, but with PREG set to 1 (unlike Template A's fully-combinational PREG=0 configuration) so the P output register is enabled and updates the product on each rising CLK edge. Zero-extend a to the 30-bit A input and b to the 18-bit B input, configure OPMODE/ALUMODE for a pure multiply (no accumulation), tie CARRYIN to 1'b0 and D to 25'b0, and slice the lower 32 bits of the registered P output as product. Because PREG(1) already registers P, product MUST be exposed as a COMBINATIONAL slice of P's lower 32 bits, never re-registered with a second always @(posedge clk) block -- doing so adds a second cycle of latency.

designs.Problem:
Design a 16x16-bit unsigned synchronous (registered) multiplier that does NOT use any dedicated DSP hardware multiplier block, meeting a tight clock constraint.

Module Name: mult_16x16_no_dsp_tight_timing
Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - a[15:0]: first unsigned operand
  - b[15:0]: second unsigned operand
Outputs:
  - product[31:0]: registered unsigned product of a and b, updated on each rising clk edge (one cycle of latency)

On each rising edge of clk, product must update to the product of the a and b values sampled at that same edge, using only general FPGA fabric logic (LUTs and fast-carry chains) -- the target device's DSP48E1 slices must NOT be used for this design. This design is intentionally clocked at a tight period (see Clock Constraint) to exercise post-synthesis timing analysis in addition to fabric-primitive checks.
designs.fabric_hint: Register only the output (e.g. always @(posedge clk) product <= a*b;), keeping the 16x16 multiply itself as combinational logic between the input ports and the output register, exactly as in mult_16x16_no_dsp. The '*' operator alone does not guarantee DSP inference is avoided under every Vivado synthesis strategy, so if you observe DSP48E1 usage, restructure the arithmetic as an explicit shift-and-add partial-product accumulation using plain adders instead. Because this design's clock period is tight, prefer a balanced partial-product adder tree (combine pairs of partial products level by level) over a single long ripple-through accumulation chain, to minimize combinational logic depth and close timing.
designs.primitive_hint: Do not structurally instantiate a DSP48E1. Generate the 16 partial products and sum them using an explicit adder tree structurally instantiating CARRY4 primitives (per the CARRY4 template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above), organized as a balanced binary reduction tree (pairwise partial-product adds combined level by level) rather than a single flat ripple-carry chain across all 16 partial products, to minimize the number of series CARRY4 stages on the critical path and meet the tight clock constraint.

designs.Problem:
Design a 16x16-bit unsigned combinational multiplier (zero-latency, no clock).

Module Name: mult_16x16_dsp_combinational
Inputs:
  - a[15:0]: first unsigned operand
  - b[15:0]: second unsigned operand
Outputs:
  - product[31:0]: combinational product output

The design must compute product = a * b as purely combinational logic (no pipeline/output register, no clock, no reset).
designs.fabric_hint: Use direct full-vector unsigned multiplication (product = a * b) with minimal surrounding logic so synthesis can infer a single DSP48E1 for 16x16 multiplication.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate one DSP48E1 configured for combinational multiplication with PREG disabled (no output register), mapping operands into A/B ports and wiring P to product[31:0] with appropriate zero-extension/truncation for unused upper bits.

designs.Problem:
Design a 128x32 single-port RAM (128 addressable locations, 32 bits wide, 4Kbit total) with synchronous write and asynchronous (combinational) read, implemented with minimum Block RAM (BRAM) usage -- i.e. the synthesis tool should map the memory onto distributed RAM (LUT-based SelectRAM) rather than a dedicated RAMB18E1/RAMB36E1 block.

Module Name: ram128x32_distributed_pressure
Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - we: write enable, when high writes din into mem[addr] on the rising clk edge
  - addr[6:0]: 7-bit address (128 locations)
  - din[31:0]: 32-bit data input
Outputs:
  - dout[31:0]: 32-bit data output, dout = mem[addr] (combinational/asynchronous read)

The read must be purely combinational (dout must reflect mem[addr] immediately, with no clocked output register), and the write must be synchronous (only committed on the rising edge of clk when we is high). Clock frequency target: 100 MHz (10 ns period).
designs.Module header:
module ram128x32_distributed_pressure (
    input         clk,
    input         we,
    input  [6:0]  addr,
    input  [31:0] din,
    output [31:0] dout
);
designs.fabric_hint: Describe the memory as a small 128-entry, 32-bit-wide register array with synchronous write and purely combinational (asynchronous) read (e.g. reg [31:0] mem [0:127]; always @(posedge clk) if (we) mem[addr] <= din; assign dout = mem[addr];), rather than a registered/synchronous-read style, so the synthesis tool maps it onto LUT-based distributed RAM (SelectRAM) instead of a dedicated Block RAM tile. Because this design has a tight LUT budget, prefer the compact distributed-RAM mapping over any wider register-file-plus-multiplexer style implementation.
designs.primitive_hint: Explicitly instantiate 32 RAM128X1S primitives (one per output data bit), analogous to the RAM32X1S template in the FPGA fabric knowledge above but using the 128-deep RAM128X1S variant (7-bit address). All 32 instances share the same 7-bit address (A0-A6 wired to addr[0]-addr[6]), WCLK wired to clk, and WE wired to we; wire each instance's D to din[i] and O to dout[i] for i = 0..31 (a generate loop is idiomatic here). Vivado's report_utilization reports these structurally-instantiated instances as RAM128X1S (Ref Name, Functional Category 'Distributed Memory'). Each RAM128X1S uses 4 LUT6 plus dedicated MUXF7/MUXF8 fabric to reach 128 addresses, so the tight LUT_USED cap in this design's hard constraints should be met if you use the primitive directly rather than building the same depth out of ordinary case-statement logic.

designs.Module header:
